key_insight: Physics-informed neural networks can optimize single-qubit quantum gates at the level of the full controlled evolution, learning control fields, state trajectories, and duration together under the Bloch equation.
engineering_relevance: This process-level approach makes quantum gate design more interpretable and adaptable, enabling hardware-aware refinement without relying on a fixed pulse ansatz or duration sweep.
method: Represent gate synthesis with a PINN constrained by the Bloch equation
Jointly learn pulse shape, Bloch-state trajectory, and total gate time
Use the learned evolution structure to diagnose and locally correct geometric-condition errors
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that optimized evolutions recover expected bounded-control structure for rotation gates and that, for a geometric gate, feedback reduced residual path error while preserving high fidelity.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated at the single-qubit level in abstracted control settings, so extension to noisy multi-qubit hardware may require additional constraints and validation.
paper_title: Evolution-Level Quantum Optimal Control of Single-Qubit Gates with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
